subject: Performance SLO & context window follow-up (FinCo)
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex@finco.com>

Cc: Sally Green <sally.green@finco.com>

Subject: Re: Intro / Demo — performance follow-up

Hi Marissa — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap from our side and next steps: 

- Our primary use case is an in-product assistant that ingests up to 6k tokens of user context (chat + docs) and returns an answer + citations. Typical output length will be ~150-400 tokens.
- Target latency: p95 < 400ms end-to-end for non-streaming responses, and p95 < 250ms when streaming is acceptable (we'd like to stream for long answers).
- Expected steady-state concurrency: 30 concurrent users during peak with peaks up to ~120 concurrent requests (burst).
- Throughput: average ~12 RPS, peak sustained ~50 RPS for short windows.
- We need guaranteed max input size: 6k tokens input and up to 1k tokens output. If higher context is needed, we can consider truncation or multi-pass retrieval.

Can you confirm whether these targets are feasible with the models we discussed (open Llama variants) and what latency impact we should expect as the context window increases? Also please share any recommended batching, caching, or quantization options to hit the p95 targets.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Product
FinCo Capital

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / Demo — performance follow-up

Alex — great to sync. Appreciate the clear targets. Short answers below and attached a one-page proposal with latency/throughput estimates.

Recap of what we heard: input context 6k tokens, output up to 1k tokens, p95 targets 400ms non-streaming / 250ms streaming, steady concurrency 30 / burst 120, peak throughput ~50 RPS.

Feasibility notes (high level):
- Model selection: For 6k context with those latency targets, we recommend a medium-sized open model (e.g., Llama 2 13B optimized + 8-bit quantization) for predictable latency. Larger models (70B) will increase p50/p95 by 2–4x for the same token lengths.
- Context window impact: latency increases roughly linearly with context length for autoregressive decoding when using naive attention; with kernel optimizations (flash attention, KV cache management) we see ~1.8x latency at 6k versus 1k for the same output length on our optimized runtime. So if p95 is 200ms at 1k context, expect ~360ms at 6k (approx).
- Streaming: streaming reduces perceived latency for the user because tokens arrive earlier, but total time-to-last-token is similar. For your 250ms streaming p95 target, we should target model+runtime p95 of ~180ms to account for network tails and client rendering.
- Batching & concurrency: to meet low tail latency at 30–120 concurrent users, we recommend small shard sizes and aggressive priority queuing for interactive routes. Batching helps throughput but increases tail latency; we'll recommend dynamic per-route batching (max batch size 8, max latency 10ms) in the attached config.
- Caching & retrieval: heavy prefix caching for repeated system prompts and retrieval results will drastically reduce average tokens processed. If 60% of tokens are cached, p95 improves by ~30–40%.

Next steps we propose:
1) Engineering workshop (30–45m) to review sample prompts and confirm token footprints — can we schedule next Tue/Wed?
2) Pilot: 2-week dedicated capacity trial to validate p95 at your concurrency profile (we'll instrument with request tracing).
3) Security questionnaire + purchase order prep (Rishi will coordinate).

Attached: redwood-performance-slo-proposal.pdf (latency estimates + config), finco-context-window-reqs.xlsx (sample tokenizations).

—
